Item: Raw Go error text is returned directly to the caller in error responses (buildErrorResponse embeds validationError.Error()); additionally, on the malformed-array-entry path, the caller's own submitted value is reflected back into the 500 response body (elementValue := fmt.Sprintf("%v", item)).

Item: Text-mode decoration does raw string concatenation of admin-configured instruction text with user content, separated only by a single space, with no structural boundary (e.g. XML-style delimiter) — a user's own prompt content sits directly adjacent to the decorator's instruction with no separation, so adversarial user text can attempt to override, negate, or blend into the decorator's instruction once both land in the same string.
Mitigations / Comments: promptdecorator.go:327,329. This is inherent to how a text-splice decorator works, not a simple bug. Prefer message-role-based decoration (already supported, structurally safer) over text splicing wherever possible; if text splicing must be supported, wrap the decorator text in a clear delimiter/marker and document that placement adjacency does not guarantee instruction precedence against adversarial input.

Item: slog.Debug logs the actual stringified content of a malformed message-array entry taken directly from the request body.
Mitigations / Comments: promptdecorator.go:356. Log a length/hash/truncated preview instead of raw payload content, even at debug level.

Item: No maxLength cap exists on configured promptDecoratorConfig.text/messages[].content (schema only sets minLength:1) nor on incoming body content size within this policy — nothing here bounds how large the decorated payload can grow.
Mitigations / Comments: policy-definition.yaml:21,44 (minLength only, no maxLength). Mostly admin-configured rather than directly attacker-controlled, but compounds with large upstream payloads. Item: The SDK's ExtractValueFromJsonpath supports wildcard ("*") path segments, but this policy's own navigatePath/setValueAtPath implementations have no wildcard handling — configuring a wildcard-shaped jsonPath here would likely misbehave, the same class of gap identified in pii-masking-regex.
Mitigations / Comments: Cross-referenced against sdk/core@v0.2.4/utils/jsonpath.go:56-77. Reject/validate wildcard-shaped jsonPath values at config time if unsupported, or implement consistent wildcard write-back support across all jsonPath-consuming policies.

Item: The client fully controls which configured template fires and all placeholder values via a template://<name>?<query> reference embedded in their own request content; values are substituted verbatim into the prompt sent upstream with no content sanitization or keyword filtering. Item: template:// references are scanned out of the CLIENT'S OWN submitted content (FindAllString with no cap on match count), and each match triggers a full template lookup+substitution. Mitigations / Comments: prompttemplate.go:226. Cap the maximum number of template:// references resolved per request, and/or cap the total expanded payload size.

Item: onUnresolvedPlaceholder defaults to "keep", which forwards the literal unresolved [[placeholder]] text upstream to the LLM instead of blocking — this is the DEFAULT behavior, not an opt-in. onMissingTemplate: passthrough (an available, non-default option) similarly forwards the literal unresolved template://... string upstream.
Mitigations / Comments: prompttemplate.go:194-207 (default keep), 264-266, 292-293. Consider a more conservative default (error) for security-sensitive deployments; clearly document the security implications of passthrough/keep in the policy docs.

Mitigations / Comments: urlguardrail.go: checkDNS (305-337), checkURL (340-359), invoked on request content extracted from client-supplied messages. Mitigations / Comments: urlguardrail.go:67 (incompleteURLAtEnd regex), 649/522 (FindAllString unbounded), 202-204 (timeout has a minimum but no maximum), 655-666 (sequential validation loop).
